correctness.rationale: PASS: The explicit normalized Padé denominator is checked against the general factorial formula. After the exact translation z=t+w (t=k+1), its cubic has one real root r in (1/2,2/3) and the conjugate pair -r/2±ib. Its positive pole R=t+r is strictly smallest in modulus. Partial fraction residues A>0 and B obey A>2|B| because an exact squared-residue difference equals 9r^4(1-r)(r^3-4r^2+10r-4)/(4(2-3r)^2)>0. Consequently c_n≥(A-2|B|)R^(-n)>0 for every independent k,n≥0. Matrix convergence and positivity follow from the matrix power series and Perron-Frobenius. Symbolic algebra and 15,914 executable tests checked, not substituted for, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: PASS under available historical evidence: The 2019 Fasi–Higham Conjecture 3.2 states the odd-denominator positivity question but does not prove the all-k cubic specialization. The 2025 Al-Mohy–Liu primary preprint studies the same [3+p/3] matrix denominator in numerical matrix-function algorithms but not its reciprocal-coefficient signs. Scardino (October 28, 2026) proves all-n only at k=0, and eventual positivity under a spectral condition for other k, so his claims do not imply all n for k≥1; his degree-five counterexamples concern a different denominator order. Comparisons with primary literature, indexed mathematical findings and accessible historical claims identified no equivalent or broader proven all-k,m=3 result. Older Padé root-asymptotic work was only bibliographically accessible, so historical priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Earlier specialized Padé zero/reciprocal-coefficient theorems may be unindexed or use transformed polynomial notation.
Driver–Temme 1998 full text could not be fetched from its CWI archival link (HTTP 403). No conclusion of noncoverage is drawn from this inaccessible document.
A mathematical self-review is not independent priority verification.

value.rationale: PASS: The exact all-degree cubic case of a named unresolved Padé reciprocal-positivity problem is substantive: it proves simultaneous positivity for infinitely many numerator degrees and all Taylor orders, including the finite initial coefficients not supplied by available eventual-positivity theorems. In numerical linear algebra it gives an exact positive-cone and sharp spectral-radius guarantee for denominators of [3+p/3] Padé matrix φ-function recovery, rather than a limited collection of low-order numerical examples. No general odd-degree theorem, matrix rational numerator guarantee, or complexity improvement is claimed.
